Here's what happened on Thursday, Nov 12 — a SEV2 incident, fully documented in the postmortem [1]:

**What broke**
- From 08:47 to 12:27 UTC (3h40), customer dashboards showed stale data [1].
- Root cause: ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB. With the 512 Mi memory limit, the ingest-worker pods OOM'd on the first large batch and crash-looped — and the change rolled out to all pods at once [1].
- Detection was slow: there was no alert on consumer lag; the first signal was a Sentry out-of-memory alert at 09:14, 27 minutes after the deploy [1][4]. Fixed by rolling back to v2.13.3 at 10:05; lag drained by 12:27 [1].

**Data loss: none**
- Events kept arriving in Kafka and were just processed late. Lior's reconciliation on Nov 13 confirmed event counts per workspace match the Kafka offsets — "Nothing lost, just late" [1][11].

**What's changing (action items)**
1. KES-431 – Page on-call when the ingest-events consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (Noa, due Nov 20) [1][12]
2. KES-432 – Ingest config changes go to a canary pool first instead of all pods (Daniel, due Nov 27) [1][2]
3. KES-433 – Raise worker memory limit to 1 Gi and add a load test on batch sizes (Lior, due Nov 27) [1]

Incident reports went to Orbitly and Zest Grocers on Nov 15 [1]; note Orbitly is claiming an SLA credit under their custom 2024 MSA, which Sam is handling as part of their renewal [2][14].
